item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it uses the established multipart helper and delegates directly to FilesService.Add, preserving centralized option, request, decoding, and error behavior.","reasons":["B implements Upload as the intended thin convenience wrapper: validate, call multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), then call s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...).","A violates the explicit requirement to route Upload through Add. It duplicates Add's option processing, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error handling, creating maintenance and semantic-drift risk.","B's multipart test verifies the field name, uploaded filename, and file content. A verifies the field and filename but never reads or checks the content.","B includes an end-to-end 429 retry test through Files.Upload, while A only adds a generic retry-transport test using a bytes.Reader and does not verify Upload itself retries."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates lower-level Add machinery instead of reusing it, contrary to the contract.","No Upload retry test and no assertion of uploaded file content.","No tests for empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures."],"risks_b":["It still lacks explicit tests for empty filename, nil content, and source-reader failures.","The retry test confirms two calls but does not inspect the multipart body on both attempts, so replayed payload integrity is not directly asserted.","The retry test does not explicitly set RetryAllMethods: true, making its relationship to the reported POST-retry configuration less clear."]}
